summary: As a simulated Stack Exchange power user, I would likely NOT buy this. The pain is real but mild — it's an annoyance, not a bleeding neck. Free alternatives like SEDE and userscripts are 'good enough' for my needs. My willingness to pay is near zero because this is a vanity/hobby metric, not something tied to my income. I might use a free version, but I would not pay a subscription for it.
strongest_points: Automated daily snapshots would save me from manually recording data or running SEDE queries every week — if I actually cared enough to track trends that closely.
Cross-site aggregation in one dashboard would be convenient since I participate in 3-5 SE sites and checking each individually is tedious.
Clean visualization would be nice for sharing my 'growth story' on social media or a personal blog, which appeals to my ego as a writer.
If it offered a free tier with basic charts and a paid tier for advanced analytics, I might use the free tier and occasionally wish I had the paid features.
weaknesses: I can already get this data for free via SEDE or the API — the friction is learning SQL, which as a power user I probably already know or can copy-paste a query.
My willingness to pay is essentially $0-$2/month. This is a vanity metric, not a revenue-driving tool. I will not pay $10/month for reputation charts.

Trust blocker: Stack Exchange changes their UI and API periodically. A third-party tracker could break at any time and I'd lose my historical data. Why trust a small SaaS with my data when SE itself is the source of truth?
The pain intensity is low (2/5). I think about my reputation maybe once a week. It's not something I need daily automated tracking for — I can check my profile when I'm curious.
Switching friction is low because I'm not switching FROM anything expensive. I'm switching from 'free manual check' to 'paid automation.' That's a hard sell.
